Chain of Infection Control

Why Hand Hygiene is Vital for Cleaning Staff

Personal Protection
👨‍⚕️ Protecting Yourself & Family

Cleaning staff handle contaminated mops, body fluids, hospital linens, and bio-medical waste bags daily.

  • Invisible pathogens cling to hands beneath fingernails and wrist folds.
  • Failure to wash hands before meals or touching your face causes severe illness.
  • Proper hand hygiene prevents hospital superbugs from reaching your home.
Patient Protection
🏥 Breaking Transmission Links

When cleaning bed rails, switches, and tables, contaminated hands can spread germs from bed to bed.

  • Patients in ICU, post-op wards, and dialysis have very fragile immunity.
  • Unwashed hands transfer resistant bacteria (MRSA, Klebsiella).
  • Your clean hands prevent life-threatening Healthcare-Associated Infections (HAIs).
Quality Accreditation
🏆 Kayakalp & NQAS Excellence

National accreditation assessors directly observe and interview sanitation staff on hygiene protocols.

  • Inspectors verify if cleaning staff execute all 6 handwash steps properly.
  • Direct impact on District Hospital Kozhencherry's Kayakalp award ranking.
  • Housekeeping hygiene compliance carries high weightage in NQAS audits.
80%
WHO & MoHFW Scientific Fact: Up to 80% of all hospital-acquired infections are transmitted directly via unwashed hands. Consistent hand hygiene by housekeeping personnel is our hospital's strongest barrier against ward outbreaks.

NQAS IPC Standard MODULE 03/10
WHO Operational Protocol Adapted For Housekeeping

The 5 Critical Moments of Hand Hygiene for Cleaning Staff

01
Before Clean Supplies
PRE-CLEANING

Before taking clean mops, clean microfiber cloths, fresh linens, or preparing fresh disinfectant solutions in the housekeeping room.

02
Entering Patient Zone
BEDSIDE ENTRY

Before touching bed rails, bedside lockers, IV stands, or tables in a patient's immediate surroundings.

03
After Body Fluid Spills
HIGH HAZARD

Immediately after cleaning blood spills, vomit, urine, bedpans, catheter drainage, or handling contaminated wet linen.

04
After Dirty Zones & Toilets
POST-SANITATION

After scrubbing washrooms, commodes, sluice rooms, or mopping sluice floor surfaces. Wash before moving into the ward corridor!

05
After Removing Gloves
MANDATORY STEP

Immediately after doffing utility or examination gloves. Gloves are not 100% leakproof; hands sweat and harbor microbes inside!

✔
Golden Housekeeping Rule: Never carry cleaning tools or move from a "dirty area" (e.g., patient washroom or isolation room) to a "clean area" (e.g., nursing counter or medicine store) without performing hand hygiene first!

SOP Protocol MODULE 04/10
WHO & NQAS Standardized Technique

The 6-Step Hand Hygiene Technique (Step-by-Step)

💧 Soap & Water: 40–60 Seconds ⚡ Hand Rub: 20–30 Seconds
01

Palm to Palm

Rub hands palm to palm vigorously in circular motion to lather soap over the entire inner hand surface.

02

Back of Hands (Dorsum)

Right palm over left dorsum with fingers interlaced, rub thoroughly. Switch and repeat for right hand.

03

Interlaced Web Spaces

Palm to palm with fingers interlaced. Clean the deep spaces and skin webbing between fingers where microbes hide.

04

Back of Fingers (Knuckles)

Interlock fingers into opposite palms with knuckles bent. Rub side-to-side to scour back of folded fingers.

05

Thumbs Rotational Rub

Clasp left thumb firmly in right palm and rotate back and forth. Switch and rotate right thumb in left palm.

06

Fingertips, Nails & Wrists

Rub clustered fingertips rotational in palm to clean under nails. Finish by rubbing both wrists before rinsing.

💡
Kayakalp Assessment Checklist: Assessors will observe cleaning staff demonstrating this full sequence. Remember the mnemonic: Palms → Backs → Web spaces → Knuckles → Thumbs → Fingertips & Wrists!
Prepared by Merlin Joy • District Hospital, Kozhencherry

Comparison Standard MODULE 05/10
Choosing the Correct Method

Soap & Water vs. Alcohol-Based Hand Rub (ABHR)

MECHANICAL WASH
Soap & Running Water
40–60 SECONDS

Mandatory In The Following Situations:

  • Visibly Soiled Hands: Hands have dust, dirt, grease, or chemical stains.
  • Body Fluid Contact: After cleaning blood, urine, vomit, or fecal spills.
  • After Cleaning Toilets: Scrubbing pans, commodes, sinks, or handling soiled mops.
  • Diarrheal Patient Wards: Caring for C. difficile or Norovirus areas (alcohol rub cannot penetrate bacterial spores).
  • Personal Hygiene: After using the staff washroom or before eating food.
*Always dry hands thoroughly using clean single-use paper towels or air dry. Never wipe on your uniform!
RAPID ANTISEPSIS
Alcohol Hand Rub (ABHR)
20–30 SECONDS

Ideal For Routine Point-of-Care Sanitization:

  • No Visible Soil: Hands feel clean but require quick microbial decontamination.
  • Moving Between Beds: When wiping bedside rails from Bed 1 to Bed 2 in a general ward.
  • Before Wearing Gloves: Quick sanitization before donning clean rubber/nitrile gloves.
  • Housekeeping Trolley: Mounted on your cleaning cart for continuous immediate use.
  • Rapid Action: Kills 99.9% of bacteria and viruses in 20 seconds.
*Rub vigorously until hands are 100% dry. Do not fan hands or wipe the sanitizer off with a rag.
⚠️
Important Distinction: Alcohol rub is fast and convenient, but it does NOT wash away physical dirt or spore-forming microbes. If hands have visible grime or blood, soap and running water is compulsory!

Staff Safety Standard MODULE 06/10
Personal Protective Equipment

PPE & Gloves: Rules, Myths & Common Errors

MYTH VS FACT
⚠️ Gloves Do NOT Replace Handwash

A common misconception among cleaning staff is believing gloves provide 100% protection without hand hygiene.

  • Gloves have microscopic pores that allow fluid and viral seepage.
  • Warm perspiration inside gloves triggers massive bacterial growth on hands.
  • Taking gloves off always touches the contaminated outer surface against skin.
  • Hand hygiene is required immediately after removing gloves!
ORDER OF ACTIONS
👐 Donning & Doffing Sequence

How to wear and remove gloves safely to prevent self-contamination during hospital sanitation rounds:

  • Before Donning: Wash hands thoroughly and dry completely before wearing gloves.
  • During Work: Never touch your eyes, nose, phone, or door handles with gloved hands.
  • Safe Doffing: Peel glove from wrist rolling inside-out. Hold with other gloved hand. Slide bare fingers inside second glove to invert both.
GLOVE SELECTION
🧪 Right Glove for the Right Task

Under Kayakalp guidelines, matching glove types to the cleaning environment is mandatory:

  • Heavy-Duty Rubber Utility Gloves: For scrubbing toilets, mopping floors, handling BMW bags, and washing contaminated mops.
  • Nitrile / Examination Gloves: For wiping patient bedside furniture and cleaning low-risk ward surfaces.
  • Wash utility gloves with soap and water, inspect for punctures, and hang dry inside-out daily.
🚫
Strict Kayakalp & NQAS Prohibition: Never spray sanitizer or rub disinfectant chemicals onto gloved hands! Alcohol degrades glove material, creates holes, and gives a false sense of security. Always discard gloves and wash hands.

BMW Rules 2016 MODULE 07/10
Kayakalp Waste Handling & Hand Protection

Bio-Medical Waste Segregation & Hand Hygiene Safeguards

Yellow Bin • Infectious
Anatomical & Soiled

Human tissues, soiled cotton, dressing gauze, plaster casts, blood-soaked swabs, expired medicine, and microbiology cultures.

Method: Incineration / Pyrolysis
Red Bin • Plastics
Recyclable Plastics

Tubing, IV bottles, syringes (without needle), urine bags, catheters, gloves, and vacutainer tubes without sharps.

Method: Autoclaving & Shredding
Blue Cardboard Box / Bin
Glassware & Implants

Medicine glass ampoules, vials, contaminated glassware, and orthopedic metal implants.

Method: Disinfection & Recycling
White Box • Sharps
Puncture-Proof Sharps

Needles, scalpels, surgical blades, lumbar puncture needles, contaminated sharp metal items.

Method: Dry Heat / Encapsulation

Housekeeping Handling Protocols for Kozhencherry Cleaning Staff:

1. Tie at 2/3 Capacity: Never overfill or press down bags with hands or feet. Tie with zip-tie or knot.
2. Never Recap Sharps: If a syringe is found on floor, use forceps and put in white container. Never touch needle tips!
3. Immediate Handwash: Wash hands with soap and water immediately after transporting bags to central storage.

Occupational Health MODULE 08/10
Staff Wellness & Disinfectant Handling

Chemical Safety, Hypochlorite Dilution & Skin Care

SODIUM HYPOCHLORITE
🧪 Dilution SOP Guidelines

Sodium Hypochlorite (Bleach) is the primary hospital disinfectant for high-risk decontamination:

  • 1% Hypochlorite (10,000 ppm): For managing active blood, body fluid spills, and HIV/Hepatitis surface cleaning.
  • 0.5% Hypochlorite (5,000 ppm): For routine floor mopping in Operation Theatres, ICUs, and Isolation wards.
  • Prepare Fresh Daily: Diluted bleach loses chlorine strength after 24 hours. Keep in opaque containers.
SKIN HEALTH
🧾 Preventing Dermatitis

Repeated handwashing and harsh chemicals strip natural skin oils, causing cracks, dryness, and eczema:

  • Dry Thoroughly: Always dry hands completely before wearing gloves to prevent fungal dermatitis.
  • Moisturizing Cream: Apply hospital-approved soothing lotion at end of shift and before going home.
  • Lukewarm/Cool Water: Never wash hands with scalding hot water; it increases skin irritation and removes protective lipids.
EMERGENCY PROTOCOL
🩸 Needle-Stick or Sharp Injury

If accidentally punctured by a discarded needle or sharp object during cleaning:

  • Wash Under Tap: Wash gently with soap and running water immediately. Do NOT squeeze or scrub the wound!
  • Do NOT Use Bleach: Never apply sodium hypochlorite or alcohol rub into puncture wounds.
  • Immediate Reporting: Report to Merlin Joy / Sister In-Charge within 2 hours for Post-Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP).
👩‍⚕️
District Hospital Kozhencherry Staff Wellness: If you experience persistent redness, itching, or cracks on your hands, report directly to the Infection Control Sister or Merlin Joy. We supply specialized barrier creams to safeguard your skin!

Audit Checklist MODULE 09/10
Kayakalp Thematic Area B & NQAS IPC Indicators

Audit Checkpoints: What Assessors Inspect at Kozhencherry

01
Washing Sink Setup

Assessors examine dedicated handwashing sinks in wards and sluice rooms.

  • Elbow-operated or sensor taps in working condition.
  • Continuous 24/7 running water with no pipe leaks.
  • Clean sink bowl free from dirt rings, stains, and debris.
02
Liquid Soap Dispensers

Strict prohibition against solid bar soaps in healthcare areas!

  • Functioning wall-mounted liquid soap dispensers.
  • Clean dispenser nozzles (no dried congealed soap).
  • Never top-off partially empty soap bottles; wash and dry bottle before refilling.
03
Drying & Waste Bin

Wet hands spread 1000 times more bacteria than dry hands!

  • Availability of clean paper towels or designated single-use cloths.
  • Foot-pedal operated waste bin located next to the washbasin.
  • Staff must not share communal damp cloth towels.
04
Housekeeping Cart

The mobile cleaning trolley is a key inspection highlight.

  • Mounted bottle of alcohol hand rub (ABHR) with valid expiry date.
  • Clear color-coded microfiber cloths (Blue for glass, Red for toilets, Yellow for tables).
  • Pictorial handwashing charts displayed in Malayalam & English.
📝
Daily Housekeeping Responsibility: Cleaning staff must inspect their assigned ward handwashing station at the start of every shift. If liquid soap or paper towels are missing, notify the store in-charge or Merlin Joy immediately!

Operational Takeaways

5 Golden Hand Hygiene Rules
For Housekeeping Heroes

1
Perform hand hygiene at all 5 housekeeping moments without fail.
2
Soap & water (40-60s) when visibly soiled; ABHR (20-30s) for routine speed.
3
Gloves do not replace hand hygiene; wash immediately after glove removal.
4
Follow BMW 4-color segregation strictly; never press down waste bags.
5
Dry hands completely to protect your skin; report injuries within 2 hours.
